display.title: The Golden Bells of Aharon's Robe: Let Your Voice Be Heard
display.summary_short: The golden bells on Aharon HaKohen's robe teach that, though children should not interrupt, their voices should ring out when they say brachos, daven and bench.
display.summary_long: A short parsha talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, from Tuesday's portion of Parshas Tetzaveh (Shemos 28:35). Uncle Yossi describes the me'il, the robe of Aharon HaKohen, with golden bells and pomegranate-shaped ornaments along its hem; a little hammer in each bell made a lovely sound, so that 'its sound shall be heard when he enters the holy place.' He draws a lesson for the soldiers of Tzivos Hashem. The old saying goes that children should be seen and not heard, and indeed there is a time to be quiet: interrupting someone, especially an older person, is disrespectful, and good derech eretz means waiting your turn. But when we say a brachah, daven or bench, our voices should be heard, because we are speaking to Hashem, and our sweet voices are like the golden bells, heavenly music to Him.
display.lesson: Don't interrupt others, but when you speak to Hashem in brachos and davening, let your voice be heard.
